themes_detail.label: Explosive graffiti surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints in CD 309 spiked to 22 THIS WEEK, a 529% increase versus the 3.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden outbreak of vandalism that may indicate a new crew activity or organized tagging campaign.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints this week vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (529% spike, z-score 6.65)
Spike emerged suddenly this week with no gradual escalation pattern
High statistical significance indicates concentrated incident rather than ambient noise
reporting_angles: Map the locations of this week's 22 complaints to identify hotspot(s) and interview residents in affected blocks
Contact NYPD/Sanitation to determine if they've identified a specific crew or organized tagging campaign

themes_detail.label: Water system emergency
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints hit 33 LAST WEEK, a 294% spike versus the 8.4-complaint weekly average, indicating potential infrastructure failure or contamination event that warrants urgent investigation into supply, pressure, or quality issues.
evidence: 33 water system complaints last week vs. 8.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (294% spike, z-score 6.16)
Water-related issues already endemic: 3,942 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (largest single category), 459 water leak complaints, 600 plumbing complaints
Spike timing suggests acute event rather than chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if there was a main break, pressure loss, or water quality alert in CD 309 last week
Interview residents about water outages, discoloration, or pressure loss and cross-reference with 311 complaint locations

themes_detail.label: Derelict vehicle crisis
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints surged to 20 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 150% spike versus the 8.0-complaint weekly average, indicating accumulating abandoned cars that may signal neglected enforcement or a worsening blight issue on residential streets.
evidence: 20 derelict vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (150% spike, z-score 7.59)
Complements existing parking issues: 2,097 illegal parking complaints over 90 days (2nd-largest complaint category)
High z-score indicates statistically anomalous event rather than normal variation
reporting_angles: Identify streets with multiple derelict vehicle complaints and photograph current conditions to show enforcement gaps
Interview NYPD/Sanitation about removal procedures and timelines; determine why spike occurred 2 weeks ago

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints hit 4 LAST WEEK, a 967% spike versus the 0.4-complaint weekly average, signaling a potential foodborne illness outbreak or inspection failures at one or more food service establishments requiring immediate health investigation.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 5.21)
Extreme statistical significance (z-score 5.21) indicates clustered event rather than random occurrence
Typical baseline near zero complaints suggests this represents an active outbreak
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which establishments generated the 4 complaints and their inspection status
Interview affected residents about timing, symptoms, and establishments visited to identify common source

themes_detail.label: Unleashed dog spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK, a 700% spike versus the 0.4-complaint weekly average, suggesting either a new dangerous animal situation or increased resident complaints about dog safety in parks or streets.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Baseline near zero suggests this represents a sharp departure from normal patterns
No geographic concentration data available from 311 data alone
reporting_angles: Map this week's 3 unleashed dog complaints to identify if concentrated in one park or neighborhood
Interview park users and residents about specific dogs/owners creating safety concerns
